batchMeta.auditNotes: Qwen re-audit after reconcile round 1 passed 40/40 questions with no remaining disagreements, ambiguities, equal options, key/explanation mismatches or leaky visuals.
batchMeta.provenanceNote: Generated by codex, independently audited by qwen, and queued for Claude final review after one reconcile round.

questions.prompt: Which body system carries oxygen and nutrients around the body?
questions.explanation: Blood in the circulatory system transports oxygen and nutrients.

questions.prompt: Which force pulls a dropped ball towards the ground?
questions.explanation: Gravity attracts the ball towards Earth.

questions.prompt: Which change occurs when chocolate softens from a solid to a liquid?
questions.explanation: Melting is the change from solid to liquid.

questions.prompt: Which object is a star?
questions.explanation: The Sun produces its own light and energy, so it is a star.

questions.prompt: Which surface usually creates the most friction for a sliding block?
questions.explanation: A rough surface has more irregularities that resist sliding.

questions.prompt: Which feature helps a fish take oxygen from water?
questions.explanation: Gills exchange gases with water.

questions.prompt: Which mixture can be separated using a magnet?
questions.explanation: A magnet attracts the iron filings but not the sand.

questions.prompt: Why should a measurement be repeated?

options.text: To remove the need for units

questions.explanation: Repeated results reveal variation and improve confidence.

questions.prompt: Which material is transparent?
questions.explanation: Clear glass transmits most visible light.

questions.prompt: Gas in a sealed syringe can be compressed more than liquid. Why?

options.text: Gas particles have larger spaces between them

questions.explanation: The spaces between gas particles can be reduced.

questions.prompt: Why do we see different Moon phases?

options.text: Earth's shadow covers it every week
We see different portions of its sunlit half

questions.explanation: The positions of Earth, Moon and Sun change the visible lit portion.

questions.prompt: Which organism is a producer in a pond food web?
questions.explanation: Algae make food using light, so they are producers.

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures mass?
questions.explanation: A balance compares or measures mass.

questions.prompt: A parachute with a larger canopy falls more slowly than a small one. What mainly explains this?
questions.explanation: The larger area interacts with more air, increasing drag.

questions.prompt: Two similar plants receive equal water. One is kept in light and one in darkness. Which observation best tests the effect of light?

options.text: Compare the colours of their pots
Count the windows in the room
Compare their new growth after one week

questions.explanation: New growth is the outcome that may respond to the different light condition.

questions.prompt: Why can salt be recovered from salt water by evaporation?

options.text: Salt evaporates and leaves the water behind
Water leaves as vapour while salt remains

questions.explanation: Water evaporates at the conditions used, leaving dissolved salt behind.

questions.prompt: Two identical globes are connected in series. One globe is removed. What happens?

options.text: The circuit opens and the other globe goes out
The other globe becomes a battery
The removed globe still completes the electric path

questions.explanation: Removing a series component breaks the only current path.

questions.prompt: A class measures plant height with different rulers and gets scattered results. What change most improves the method?

options.text: Use the same ruler and measuring point
Round every value to the nearest centimetre

questions.explanation: A consistent tool and reference point reduce method variation.

questions.prompt: Rounded pebbles are found downstream while angular rocks occur upstream. What process best explains the difference?

options.text: Gravity makes new corners during transport

questions.explanation: Moving water tumbles rocks so collisions wear away sharp edges.

questions.prompt: A sealed fizzy drink loses bubbles faster when warm. Which explanation is best?

options.text: The liquid completely evaporates from the bottle
Gas escapes more readily from the warmer liquid

questions.explanation: Dissolved gas is less retained as the liquid warms and escapes more quickly.

questions.prompt: Muscles can pull on bones but cannot push them.
questions.explanation: Muscles shorten to pull, so opposing muscles are used for opposite movements.

questions.prompt: A force can change an object's speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Forces can accelerate, slow or turn an object.

questions.prompt: Dissolving salt in water destroys the salt permanently.
questions.explanation: The salt remains in the solution and can be recovered by removing water.

questions.prompt: The Sun appears to move across the sky mainly because Earth rotates.
questions.explanation: Earth's rotation changes our viewing direction during the day.

questions.prompt: A prediction and a conclusion serve exactly the same purpose.
questions.explanation: A prediction is made before testing; a conclusion interprets evidence afterwards.

questions.prompt: Every inherited feature is completely unaffected by the environment.
questions.explanation: Many features result from both inheritance and environmental conditions.

questions.prompt: Sound can travel through solids as well as gases.
questions.explanation: Vibrations can pass between particles in solids, liquids and gases.

questions.prompt: One unusual result should always be deleted without investigation.
questions.explanation: An unusual result should be checked, repeated and explained before any decision to exclude it.

questions.prompt: Which TWO features help birds fly?
questions.explanation: Low mass and a streamlined body reduce the effort and drag involved in flight.

questions.prompt: Which TWO changes usually increase friction?
questions.explanation: Roughness and a larger pressing force increase resistance between surfaces.

questions.prompt: Which TWO methods can separate an insoluble solid from water?

options.text: Using a magnet for any solid

questions.explanation: Filtration traps an insoluble solid in the filter. The mixture can also be left until the solid settles, then the clear water can be carefully poured off by decanting.

questions.prompt: Which TWO observations would support the claim that a habitat is becoming drier?
questions.explanation: A sustained moisture decrease and a community shift both support long-term drying.

questions.prompt: Which TWO variables should be controlled when comparing paper-towel absorbency?
questions.explanation: Piece size and available water must be equal; brand is changed and absorption is measured.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about food webs are correct?

options.text: One organism may have several food sources
Removing a species can affect several others
Every animal eats only one species
Energy cycles back to the Sun

questions.explanation: Food webs contain multiple feeding links, so a species change can spread through the web.

questions.prompt: Which TWO results make a claim more trustworthy?

options.text: Results chosen because they match the prediction

questions.explanation: Repetition and representative sampling strengthen evidence; selective reporting does not.

questions.prompt: Which TWO changes involve energy being absorbed by the substance?
questions.explanation: Melting and evaporation require energy input; freezing and condensation release energy.

questions.prompt: Order these parts of a food chain from the original energy source to the top consumer.
questions.explanation: Sunlight is captured by grass, which is eaten by a grasshopper, which can be eaten by a kookaburra.

questions.prompt: Order the stages as a sound reaches a listener.
questions.explanation: A source vibrates, the vibration travels through air, the eardrum moves, and signals are interpreted by the brain.

questions.prompt: Order the steps for testing which soil drains fastest.
questions.explanation: Prepare equal samples, add equal water, record each drainage time, then compare results.

items.text: Place equal soil amounts in identical funnels
Record the time for each sample

questions.prompt: Order these water-cycle processes starting with ocean water becoming vapour.
questions.explanation: Evaporation is followed by condensation, precipitation, then run-off back to the ocean.

items.text: Run-off returns water to the ocean
